# Flowie

> Flowie is a keyboard-first outliner. You can zoom into any bullet, link or mirror it elsewhere, add images, keep a daily journal, and write LaTeX. Your notes and images stay on your device. Flowie is free software under GPL-3.0-or-later, written in Rust on GPUI, with English and Simplified Chinese (简体中文) interfaces.

Key facts:

- Runs on macOS 13 or later (Apple silicon or Intel), with previews for Windows 10 or 11 x64 and Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.35 or later). Or [build from source]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/building.md).
- See the [desktop installation guide]({{ '/download.html' | absolute_url }}) for packages, checksums, and how to upgrade from a release candidate. On macOS, use `brew install --cask wesleyel/tap/flowie` (tracks the latest published version, including RCs) or get the signed, sandboxed version from the [Mac App Store]({{ site.app_store_url }}).
- Import and export OPML, Markdown and plain text. Flowie's OPML keeps internal links and mirrors. To move images, use a `.flowie` package or keep the `images` folder with the Markdown export.
- Share a branch as a `.flowie` file. The recipient can preview it, pick a location, and merge updates. Search `is:new` to find unread imports.
- Write inline `$…$` and display `$$…$$` LaTeX (KaTeX-compatible). Flowie renders it as you type.
- Connect AI assistants through the built-in MCP server (`Flowie mcp`, stdio). Settings → Agent controls read and write access. Pass bullet IDs as UUIDs or unique hexadecimal prefixes. See the [MCP guide]({{ site.github_url }}/blob/main/docs/mcp.md).
- Customize keyboard shortcuts and mouse side buttons. Use quick open to jump to any bullet, or type `/` for commands.

## Docs
